evidence.title: Turmeric - wound care
evidence.excerpt: CCRAS wound-care guidance documents turmeric in oil for abrasions and small cuts as part of traditional wound-care guidance.
evidence.authority: CCRAS, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India

evidence.title: Aloe - wound healing
evidence.excerpt: CCRAS wound-care guidance documents aloe for wound healing and its use as a natural dressing.
evidence.authority: CCRAS, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India

evidence.title: Neem - wound dressing
evidence.excerpt: CCRAS wound-care guidance documents neem oil in wound-care and dressing contexts.
evidence.authority: CCRAS, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India

evidence.title: Tulsi - cough, fever and digestive use
evidence.excerpt: CCRAS home-remedy guidance documents Tulsi preparations for cough, fever and digestion, including juice and decoction preparations.
evidence.authority: CCRAS, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India

evidence.title: Ginger - cough and fever preparations
evidence.excerpt: CCRAS traditional home-remedy guidance documents ginger in preparations associated with cough and fever.
evidence.authority: CCRAS, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India

evidence.title: Guduchi - fever decoction
evidence.excerpt: CCRAS guidance documents Guduchi, also called Giloya, prepared as a decoction in traditional fever-related guidance.
evidence.authority: CCRAS, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India

evidence.title: Licorice - cough
evidence.excerpt: CCRAS guidance documents liquorice, also called Mulethi, in traditional guidance for dry cough.
evidence.authority: CCRAS, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India

evidence.title: Ashwagandha - traditional use and stress context
evidence.excerpt: CCRAS documents Ashwagandha root in Indian traditional medicine and discusses its traditional and researched use in stress-related contexts.
evidence.authority: CCRAS, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India

evidence.title: Amla - medicinal plant identity
evidence.excerpt: The Ministry of Ayush e-Charak medicinal-plant resource lists Amla, Emblica officinalis, and identifies the fruit as the plant part used.
evidence.authority: National Medicinal Plants Board, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India

evidence.title: Brahmi - medicinal plant identity
evidence.excerpt: The Ministry of Ayush e-Charak medicinal-plant resource lists Brahmi, Bacopa monnieri, and identifies the whole plant as the plant part used.
evidence.authority: National Medicinal Plants Board, Ministry of Ayush, Government of India
